result.summary: Independently re-verified REQ-026 (T-24h 'Still coming?' reconfirmation + T-3h route/QR reminder jobs, GitHub issue #29, depends_on REQ-025) at commit 0f2e2e6, branch feature/WF02-REQ-026. Did not trust TEST-RUNNER's Step 4 report, requirement_status.yaml history, or any prior gate's summary as a substitute for my own re-derivation. 1. Read docs/agents/design/REQ-026.md and decisions/0007-doors-time-in-t3h-reminder.md in full against all 10 ACs, then read the shipped code directly and confirmed it matches line-for-line: domain/event.ts's findDoorsAgendaItem (kind==='doors' find, null on no match, per §3.2's table); domain/registration.ts's getRegistrationAdmissionAndEvent/decideReconfirmOutcome/reconfirmRegistration (only reconfirmed_at written, admission never touched, first-match-wins table exactly as §4); domain/notification.ts's sendLedgeredNotification step 5 (skip->skipped-stale with NO sender call, text->send, photo->sendPhoto, exactly §1.2's table); scheduler/reminderJobs.ts's composeReminder24h/composeReminder3h (exact §5.1/§5.2 field order, doors line built with formatDateTimeInTimezone(new Date(doorsItem.at), event.chapterTimezone, lang) -- the IDENTICAL function/argument shape domain/event.ts's buildEventCardContent uses for its own agendaLines mapping, confirmed by reading both call sites side by side); handlers/reminder24h.ts's confirm/decline handlers (ownership check via decideReconfirmOutcome/withdrawRegistration, non-disclosing refusedNotFound reply on not-owner/not-found, decline reuses the now-exported sendPromotionNotification unchanged); index.ts's bot.init()-before-startScheduledJobs sequencing and the two new callbackQuery registrations, exactly per §8. 2. Re-ran npm run lint myself: 0 errors, 2 pre-existing apps/web LCP warnings (Footer.tsx, Nav.tsx) unrelated to this diff. Re-ran npm run build myself: apps/web (Next.js/Turbopack) and apps/bot (tsc) both clean. Stood up my own scratch Postgres (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, port 55432), ran npx drizzle-kit migrate myself (applied cleanly, no doors_at/doorsAt column anywhere in the 6 migration files), then npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism from the repo root: 23 files / 255 tests passed, 0 failed -- matches TEST-RUNNER's count exactly (without the DB up, 73 DB-backed cases report skipped rather than failed, confirming the count is real and not inflated). 3. Independent re-verification with my own fresh fixtures, never reusing BACKEND-DEV's/TEST-DESIGNER's/TEST-RUNNER's scratch scripts: - AC3 genuine two-process kill-then-restart: wrote my own apps/bot/scratch-rv-p1.ts/scratch-rv-p2.ts (deleted after use). p1 built a fresh fixture (chapter Asia/Almaty, a real createEvent+publishEvent, a real registerForEvent call, event starting 23.5h out -- inside the 24h window), called makeReminder24hJob(...).run(evaluationTime), exited 0 (pid 7984). Direct query after p1: exactly 1 notification_ledger row, delivery file exactly 1 line. p2 (separate npx tsx invocation, fresh Pool/drizzle instance sharing no JS heap with p1) re-ran the identical job against the same candidate: ledger rows for the registration still exactly 1, total delivery lines across BOTH processes still exactly 1 (same pid 7984 as p1's -- sender never called again), registration admission still 'admitted'. PASS, independently reproduced. - AC7 spot-checked TEST-RUNNER's own committed fixture (reminderJobs.db.test.ts, 'AC7 (spec's own fixture)' block, America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires/en/doors label 'Registration & drinks') by reading it directly rather than re-authoring a duplicate: confirms exact `.toBe()` (not `.toContain()`) equality between the T-3h caption's extracted doors-line text and buildEventCardContent's own agendaLines entry for the identical doors item -- genuine byte-for-byte identity, not merely a substring match. Re-ran it in isolation (`-t "AC7|AC8"`): 10 passed. - AC8 spot-checked the same file's 'AC8 (spec's own fixture)' block (agenda kinds workshop/afterparty, distinct vocabulary from BACKEND-DEV's own networking/close precedent) -- confirms message.caption excludes catalog.reminder3h.doorsLabel and both non-doors items' own formatted times (guarded so a coincidental time collision with startsAt can't produce a false pass), includes only the start line. Genuine kind==='doors' equality test, not a loose 'any agenda item' match. Passed in the same isolated run above. - Forged-callback non-authorization: read and re-ran apps/bot/src/handlers/reminder24h.forgery.test.ts directly (3 passed in isolation): (1) an attacker with NO registration of their own sends reminder24h:confirm: -> non-disclosing refusedNotFound reply, victim's admission/reconfirmedAt untouched, zero registration.reconfirm audit rows for the victim's id; (2) an attacker WITH their own separate registration sends reminder24h:decline: -> same non-disclosing reply, victim's seat NOT freed, attacker's own row untouched (no silent redirect), zero registration.withdraw audit rows for the victim's id; (3) AC2 order-of-operations: decline-then-confirm on the same registrationId -> the second (confirm) call is refused (refusedNotEligible), never silently reconfirms a withdrawn registration. Real grammY bot.handleUpdate dispatch throughout, real Postgres, own tg_id range (990_000_000+). - AC9: git grep 'doors_at' and 'doorsAt' across the whole repo myself -- the only hit is a pre-existing comment at apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts:232 ('No doors_at column exists anywhere (PRD 5)') documenting the REJECTED design, not a real column; confirmed by reading every one of the 6 committed .sql migration files in apps/bot/drizzle/ directly -- none contains 'doors'. No new migration file exists in this diff. 4. Spot-checked REQ-025's S9/S10 and REQ-022/023's withdrawal/promotion paths still hold after this run's extensions (not a full re-derivation, per Step 5's instructions -- REVIEWER/SECURITY-REVIEWER already did that): re-ran notification.test.ts, registration.test.ts, registration.db.test.ts, and withdraw.test.ts against my scratch DB filtered to S9/S10/AC1-AC4 -- 14 passed, 0 failed. sendLedgeredNotification's steps 1-4 (user lookup, unconditional blocked check, classification-gated broadcastOptIn check, the atomic ledger INSERT) are unchanged from REQ-025, confirmed by reading the current file directly. 5. Confirmed full requirement scope: git diff master...HEAD --stat lists exactly the design-doc-listed files (domain/event.ts + test, domain/notification.ts + test, domain/registration.ts + new db test, domain/reminders.ts (new), handlers/reminder24h.ts (new) + 2 test files (new), handlers/withdraw.ts's export/wrapper diff, i18n/en.ts+ru.ts+types.ts, index.ts's sequencing diff, scheduler/rateLimiter.ts, scheduler/reminderJobs.ts (new) + db test (new), the design doc, the test spec, ISS-0023, and this run's own handoffs/test-report) -- nothing stray, 35 files, no files outside the allowed root set. git grep for TODO/FIXME/XXX across every REQ-026-touched source file: zero matches. git status --porcelain clean before and after this handoff (scratch Postgres container+volume and my own two scratch AC3 scripts/artifacts all torn down). 6. docs/agents/requirements.yaml's REQ-026 entry: status still 'pending' -- correct, since DOC-UPDATER (Step 6) has not run yet; not stale relative to what actually shipped once flipped. 7. Filed-issue judgment: ISS-0013 (MAJOR, no CI Postgres service) and ISS-0020 (MAJOR, REQ-018 staff.ts blocked-user gap) both pre-date this run, are unrelated to REQ-026's own correctness, and are explicitly out of scope per the task context. ISS-0013 is a standing CI-infrastructure gap I compensated for exactly as TEST-RUNNER did, by standing up and migrating my own scratch Postgres. ISS-0014 through ISS-0019, ISS-0021, ISS-0022, and this run's own ISS-0023 (the AC4 test-spec construction TEST-RUNNER found and reconstructed correctly, per its own issues[] entry) are all MINOR test-spec/test-infrastructure wording-precision issues that do not touch the shipped code's actual correctness. None of the filed issues should block this release. Overall: every independent check -- lint, build, the full 255-test suite from the repo root (both with and without the scratch DB, confirming the skip/pass boundary is real), my own two-process AC3 kill test, a direct read-and-isolated-rerun of the committed AC7/AC8/forged-callback fixtures, a direct git-grep for doors_at/doorsAt across the whole repo and all 6 migration files, and a spot-check of REQ-025/022/023's still-passing tests -- agrees with all prior gates (CODE-DESIGNER/VALIDATOR, BACKEND-DEV, REVIEWER, SECURITY-REVIEWER, TEST-DESIGNER/VALIDATOR, TEST-RUNNER). No half-implemented scope, no stray TODOs, clean git tree, all design-doc-listed files present.
